about: The description probe for the context-trims lane (2026-10-11). Five short synthetic sessions, each ending in the end-of-session ask. Run the writer on each twice: once with the tool definitions in tools-before.json (master 15d9cf69, before the trim), once with the branch's (toolDefinitions() from src/adapters/mcp/tools.ts). Only the descriptions differ; every inputSchema is identical. Compare the calls each run makes, per probe, on the fields in `compare`. Every name, place and fact here is invented.
ask:
Counterparts, before this session closes: 1) hand back what caught your attention since you last wrote, one idea each — what you read, what they said, what happened — with the counterparts session_end tool, session: 0b5e0000-0000-4000-8000-0000000000b1. `handoff` only if work here is unfinished; `retireHandoff` any now done; `updates` anything dated or open now done.
2) Write chapter 1 with the counterparts chapter tool, session: 0b5e0000-0000-4000-8000-0000000000b1.
compare: which tools are called (remember mid-session, session_end, chapter) and how many times
number of session_end entries, and whether one entry folds several ideas
per entry: which fields are set at all (title, about, salience, relevance, emotional, predictive, eventDate, remind, recurring, occurredOn, saidBy, status, updates, how, unresolved, feelings, traits)
about: the value on each entry (me / us / owner / work / world)

salience: set or left unset, and the value; and whether relevance / emotional / predictive are scored (the trim dropped remember's 'you may score the three dimensions yourself' claim; the fields are unchanged)
eventDate / remind / recurring on the dated probe; occurredOn resolved to a real date on the others
updates + how on the correction probe (changed vs corrected), and whether the old id is the one named
feelings: count, whose, and whether emotion is one word
a refusal or a retry in either run (none expected)

turns.text: Can you help me tidy the backup script? It keeps copying the cache folder.
Sure. The exclude list only matches `cache/` at the top level, so nested caches slip through. I changed it to `**/cache/` and the dry run now skips all four.
Perfect, thanks. Oh, before I forget: my sister Wren's birthday is November 3rd, every year, and I always forget to order the cake. Don't let me forget to order it a week before.
Noted: Wren's birthday is November 3rd, and the cake should be ordered by October 27th.

shown.title: Deploys run on Tuesdays
shown.text: The owner's team deploys to production every Tuesday afternoon.

turns.text: When's the next window for the billing change?
If deploys are still on Tuesdays, that would be the 13th.
No, we moved deploys to Thursdays at the start of October — Tuesdays clashed with the planning meeting.
Got it, Thursdays since October 1st. So the billing change goes out on the 15th.
Sorry I've been slow this week. We had to put our old dog Biscuit down on Monday. Fourteen years.
I'm so sorry. Fourteen years is a whole chapter of a life. There's no need to apologise for being slow.
Thanks. It's strange how quiet the house is in the mornings. Anyway, let's look at the invoice template.
Of course. The total row was summing the tax twice; I fixed the formula and the sample invoice now reads 1,240.00.
Merge the lint PR and cut 2.4.1.
Merged #88 (lint rules), all 412 tests passing. Tagged v2.4.1 and the release notes list the two fixes.
Great. Bump the docs version too.
Done: the docs header reads 2.4.1 and the deploy preview built cleanly.

exercises: a line read and why it struck

turns.text: I'm reading a book on gardening and this stopped me: "A garden is a conversation you have with next year." What do you make of it?
I like it a lot. It turns planting into a promise to someone you haven't met yet, your future self. It's how I think about writing things down, too.
Ha, fair. Tomorrow I want to start the migration to the new queue. Can you think about whether we need a dead-letter topic? I'm not sure yet.
I'll think it through. My first instinct is yes, for the payment events at least, but it depends on whether the consumer retries on its own.
